phase: Private Android log capture diagnoses Gmail code-loading and GMS version gaps

changes.capture: Opt-in Android Log sink requiring an app-owned 0700 directory, 0600 regular file, no final symlinks or hardlinks, nonblocking file lock, 4096-byte records and 8 MiB total cap
changes.activation: WESTLAKE_GOOGLE_PRIVATE_LOGS=1 and WESTLAKE_ANDROID_LOG_CAPTURE_DIR; absent opt-in preserves muted logs
changes.sharedLogging: No stderr or HiLog fallback on sink failure

inferenceLimits: The private capture reveals concrete loading/version failures; it does not establish either as the sole mailbox blocker.
These errors are not evidence of Google rejecting a newly issued Gmail token.
Gmail disables one of its own logger backends; private capture is incomplete and may drop contended or capped messages.
Version numbers are not overridden. Updating official GMS requires revalidating pinned worker routing.
A native probe outside the app SELinux context can open the APK after dropping to the client UID. Unix UID permissions alone are not established as the cause of AssetManager failure.
privacy: Only fixed outcomes and public code identifiers. Raw app logs remain in private test storage and are not published.
